newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Call spreads traded in British Petroleum.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Call spreads traded in British Petroleum.

text.p: Stock options in British Petroleum were active on Tuesday owing to various call spreads established by a number of traders, dealers said.
One of the largest deals was a diagonal bear spread from the sale of 1,000 October 650 calls at 46p, along with the purchase of 1,000 January 700 calls at 24p.

For maximum profit at the October expiry, BP shares need to fall below 650p when the short calls will be worthless. The long calls will then be held in the belief the shares can climb higher. In this way, the strategy is a means of owning long-dated calls cheaply.
In another deal, 750 lots in the same options series were traded. Also, there were sellers of 500 October 650 calls at about 47p ahead of next Wednesday's expiry.
By 1509 GMT, BP shares were up 1/2p to 700p.
Over in automotive engineer LucasVarity, the main deal was from a buyer of 750 November 240 puts at 6p.

In mobile phone group Vodafone a short strangle was the main trade from the sale of 500 January 220 puts at 8p and 500 Jnauary 240 calls at 6p. A maximum profit of 14p will be made if the shares stay between 220p-240p by the expiry date.
Vodafone shares added a penny to 228-1/2p.

The major deals concerning the FTSE 100 index options were from traders taking a view on market volatility such as that from a trader buying 700 December 4050 calls at 84-1/2p who also sold December FTSE futures at 4055.
By 1509 GMT, cash FTSE was up 5.9 points at 4037.4 while December futures were up nine points at 4078.
